newsitem.title: USA: Malone cuts Treasury budget, vows same for Mass..
newsitem.headline: Malone cuts Treasury budget, vows same for Mass..

text.p: Vowing to keep state spending levels with the rate of inflation, Massachusetts Treasurer Joe Malone highlighted what could be a key issue in the 1998 Republican gubernatorial primary, State House News Service reported.

At a Tuesday news conference in the Treasurer's office -- held to announce a decline in the Treasury's own spending -- Malone was peppered by questions on his strategy for distinguishing himself from his incumbent GOP opponent, acting Gov. Paul Cellucci.
One big part of the strategy, Malone hinted, would be a promise not to let state spending outpace the rate of inflation.

"The challenge going forward is not to simply balance the budget. It's to keep the budget from growing faster than inflation," the treasuer said. "If we continue increasing the budget at twice the rate of inflation, we will have planted the seeds of our next fiscal crisis by increasing the size of government beyond our ability to pay for it."

Malone's words were a less-than-veiled dig at Cellucci, who, as lieutenant governor, worked closely with former Gov. William Weld from 1991 until last week. During the Weld administration, the state budget grew 29 percent, over twice the rate of inflation for the Boston area between 1991 and 1997.

In the past, Weld administration officials have explained budget increases as the result of a healthy economy and greater tax revenues; officials said most new funds are funnelled to cities and towns and do not represent a growth in the state bureacracy.

But Malone maintains his experience with Treasury's budget -- which oversees the State Lottery and the state's pension funds -- illustrates a principle that can be applied to state government as a whole.
Since he took office in 1990, Malone said the Treasury has reduced spending by 55 percent.
